title: Detecting acute pain signals from human EEG
authors: G Sun, Z Wen, D Ok, L Doan, J Wang, Z S Chen et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: source-localized EEG features and sequential state-space pain-onset detection
feature_definition: Unsupervised state-space detector using localized ROI EEG to detect onset of acute pain, compared with SVM.
prediction_rationale: An onset detector estimates pain occurrence from brain activity, complementary to rating-level prediction.
verified_result_metric: Paper reports feasibility across two EEG datasets and cross-subject/cross-modality tests versus SVM; no numeric accuracy captured in the inspected abstract/source excerpts.
prediction_target: Presence/onset of acute experimentally induced pain, not continuous subjective rating.
validation_design: Two EEG datasets with cross-subject and cross-modality evaluation; source localization and sequential modeling.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: The primary paper links to public OSF Brain mediators of pain study data; the OSF record describes BrainVision EEG and perception-condition numeric ratings for 60 painful stimuli/condition at three intensity levels. This verifies public EEG and ratings, not that every analysis subset is identical.
relevance_limitations: Published method depends on source localization and temporal context; the linked EEG is 1000-Hz/65-channel in the cited dataset description, unlike the target 128-Hz sparse montage. Onset detection is not a pain-intensity regression target.

title: Selective and replicable neuroimaging-based indicators of pain discriminability
authors: Zhang et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Evoked-potential response amplitude and latency; pain AUC
feature_definition: Differences in N2/P2 peak amplitude and latency; signal-detection-theory AUC operationalizes an individual’s pain discriminability.
prediction_rationale: Inference: evoked EEG response features may estimate how sensitively an individual distinguishes pain intensity, not moment-to-moment pain itself.
verified_result_metric: LASSO-predicted AUC correlated with measured pain AUC: Pearson r=0.536 in Dataset 1 and r=0.423 in Dataset 2 (both p<0.0001). These are correlations, not R²/accuracy.
prediction_target: Individual pain-intensity discriminability (AUC).
validation_design: Three EEG cohorts (N=114,111,141); exploratory Dataset 1 and replication in Datasets 2/3; pain-selectivity assessed against non-pain sensory modalities.
open_access_status: Open-access full text (PMC; CC BY-NC-ND).
data_evidence: Linked EEG dataset paper lists raw BIDS records including ds005292; this specific data page describes trialwise pain ratings.
relevance_limitations: Peak-based, stimulus-locked feature design requires event-aligned epochs and broad scalp electrodes; article’s AUC target is not a pain rating forecast and its evidence is not based on 5-s resting windows.

title: Chronic neuropathic pain: EEG data in eyes open and eyes closed with painDETECT and brief pain inventory reports
authors: Daniela M. Zolezzi, Norberto E. Naal-Ruiz, Luz María Alonso-Valerdi, David I. Ibarra-Zarate
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Public resting EEG resource for candidate PAC, phase connectivity and feature-stability analyses
feature_definition: Raw 250-Hz EEG from 36 chronic neuropathic-pain patients (5-min eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions) with BPI and painDETECT questionnaires; paper reports bandwidth 0.1–100 Hz.
prediction_rationale: Could test whether within-session phase/PAC summaries carry information about patient questionnaire pain scores; this is a proposed reanalysis, not a result of the data descriptor.
verified_result_metric: Not applicable (dataset item; no prediction result claimed).
prediction_target: Proposed patient-level BPI/painDETECT severity or questionnaire-defined pain features
validation_design: Dataset includes 36 patients; analyses need subject-level splits to avoid window-level leakage and independent validation before clinical claims.
open_access_status: Open-access data descriptor (CC BY; PMC)
data_evidence: The data article links Mendeley repository versions and identifies raw electrophysiological signals plus questionnaire/demographic files; repository metadata identifies original data and files.
relevance_limitations: Resting state, not stimulus-locked pain; only 36 patients; five-second window labels would replicate a subject’s fixed clinical scores and are not independent. Verify channel layout for network connectivity; >40-Hz analyses require changing pipeline filters, and >64-Hz content is unavailable at 250-Hz sampling.

title: EEG frequency band analysis in chronic neuropathic pain: A linear and nonlinear approach to classify pain severity
authors: Daniela M. Zolezzi; Luz María Alonso-Valerdi; David I. Ibarra-Zarate
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Approximate entropy (ApEn) and absolute EEG band power
feature_definition: ApEn (pattern-based signal irregularity) and absolute power estimated in delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma bands at 22 scalp electrodes, using one-minute segments; chronic neuropathic pain severity grouped from Brief Pain Inventory ratings.
prediction_rationale: Authors tested whether nonlinear EEG signal dynamics/strength features separate pain severity groups better than absolute band power. The result is group differentiation rather than a validated out-of-sample pain predictor.
verified_result_metric: Paper reports ApEn group differences in most bands and conditions (p <= 0.0001) and notable clustering of pain groups using theta-, alpha- and beta-band ApEn. This is inferential/group-separation evidence, not verified held-out accuracy, correlation or R².
prediction_target: Low/moderate/high chronic neuropathic pain severity from Brief Pain Inventory; no prospective prediction endpoint.
validation_design: Cross-sectional feature comparison in 36 chronic neuropathic pain participants; 13-person healthy-control EEG database used as reference. Features derived from 10 one-minute observations per patient; Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn tests and unsupervised clustering described. No independent cohort or subject-held-out predictive validation verified.
open_access_status: Open-access article page/full text at ScienceDirect; article page identifies Creative Commons access.
data_evidence: Paper states its 36-patient database is publicly available; the linked Mendeley v4 page offers a public 529 MB download with individual patient .gdf recordings, demographics/questionnaires and channel labels. The companion data descriptor confirms these are raw electrophysiological recordings (250 Hz, 22 channels) paired with BPI/painDETECT reports. The 13 control participants come from a separate database; do not imply they are all contained in Mendeley dataset yj52xrfgtz. Access-review detail: public raw EEG verified
relevance_limitations: Relevant original pain-severity EEG analysis with public raw signals and central C3/Cz/C4 leads. However, its 1-min feature segments, 250-Hz 0.1–100-Hz acquisition and broad montage differ from 5-s, 128-Hz, 1–40-Hz workflows. BPI-derived groups and within-sample clustering do not prove calibrated individual pain prediction. It shares the Zolezzi cohort with the 2024 Ryu and Barbosa papers and the 2023 dataset descriptor; cohort reuse is not independent replication.

title: Interindividual variability and individual stability of pain- and touch-related neuronal gamma oscillations
authors: E Valentini et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: pain-evoked gamma-band oscillations and within-person stability
feature_definition: Gamma response prevalence, magnitude, and repeatability following noxious pain and innocuous touch stimulation.
prediction_rationale: Characterizes whether pain-related gamma features are stable enough to function as individual biomarkers.
verified_result_metric: Paper reports marked between-person variability and individual stability in one dataset, with gamma responses evident only in a subset; no pain-rating prediction accuracy verified.
prediction_target: Pain-evoked response reproducibility/individual trait, not a validated rating predictor.
validation_design: Two EEG datasets; 48-person pain/touch dataset linked to public OSF and a repeated-session dataset; study assesses repeatability and variability.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: Paper links the 48-participant pain/touch EEG dataset to OSF jw8rv; article methods include pain ratings. This repository is for this gamma-stability dataset, not Nickel et al. 2017 tonic heat.
relevance_limitations: Gamma frequencies above 40 Hz are removed by the target filter and most are above 64-Hz Nyquist. Gamma response variability cautions against assuming this feature is universal.

title: Pain- and touch-related neuronal gamma oscillation EEG dataset (OSF jw8rv)
authors: E Valentini et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: raw EEG, pain/touch event-related gamma, trial ratings
feature_definition: Public 48-participant EEG dataset with painful laser and matched tactile trials; paper also reports a separate repeated-session dataset.
prediction_rationale: Enables analysis of gamma response variability, stability, and relation to single-trial pain ratings.
verified_result_metric: Publicly linked dataset contains 48 healthy participants; 75 laser-pain and 75 touch trials, ratings 0–10 after each; no dataset prediction metric.
prediction_target: Pain/touch intensity ratings and event-related gamma response features.
validation_design: Single-session dataset of 48 participants; the linked study also discusses a distinct two-session 22-person dataset, do not assume both are in this OSF record.
open_access_status: Public OSF project; article open access
data_evidence: Valentini et al. explicitly link jw8rv and describe its 48 healthy participants, pain/touch paradigms, and ratings. This is distinct from Nickel et al. 2017 tonic-heat data.
relevance_limitations: Gamma above 40 Hz is removed by target filter; 64-Hz Nyquist prevents higher components. Pain and touch blocks, trial events, full montage and sampling must be checked; only C3/C4/Cz remain in target pipeline.

title: 1/f in chronic pain: raw EEG datasets linked to the preregistered aperiodic analysis
authors: Cristina Gil Ávila; Markus Ploner; linked cohort contributors
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Resting-state raw BIDS EEG with clinical pain labels; source data for periodic/aperiodic and alpha analyses
feature_definition: Public OSF project joins/references raw EEG cohorts; preregistration identifies eyes-open/closed five-minute resting state recordings and pain ratings.
prediction_rationale: Raw EEG tied to pain intensity and case/control labels permits reproducible spectral-power and aperiodic feature tests; no standalone prediction is claimed for this repository.
verified_result_metric: Dataset item; no model metric applies.
prediction_target: Cohort diagnosis and pain intensity labels linked to EEG; not a model result.
validation_design: Public multi-cohort dataset resource; study article analyzed 149 pain participants and 115 controls; source cohort count and inclusion rules differ.
open_access_status: Public OSF projects; preregistration states there are no dataset access restrictions.
data_evidence: OSF qgfma is public and links the raw-data cohort projects; preregistration xshmy explicitly lists raw BIDS-EEG URLs srpbg, a8bpx and qgfma, states public/no restrictions, and ties them to this chronic-pain study. The fetched srpbg/a8bpx OSF pages are Public Projects with study-identifying records and raw-data components/folders (their folder listings show 0 B; file bytes were not independently downloaded).
relevance_limitations: 64-channel raw BIDS EEG, 1000 Hz original sampling; original paper uses eyes-closed five-minute sessions, source reconstruction and mPFC. Requires montage mapping, preprocessing, timing and baseline audit. Only C3/C4/Cz and five-second 1–40 Hz model cannot reproduce source-localized frontal alpha/aperiodic analysis.

title: Resting-state electroencephalography delta and theta bands as compensatory oscillations in chronic neuropathic pain: a secondary data analysis
authors: Sara Pinto Barbosa; Ygor Nascimento Junqueira; Milena Apetito Akamatsu; Lucas Murrins Marques; Adriano Teixeira; Matheus Lobo; Mohamed H Mahmoud; Walid E Omer; Kevin Pacheco-Barrios; Felipe Fregni
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Relative EEG band power (delta, theta, alpha, beta and sub-bands)
feature_definition: Resting eyes-closed relative power calculated with FFT from 5-second windows with 50% overlap; regional central, frontal and parietal power features analyzed against BPI pain intensity and interference outcomes.
prediction_rationale: The secondary analysis asks whether resting EEG spectral signal strength relates to pain severity/interference in neuropathic pain. Findings are associations from a small cross-sectional sample, not a validated forecast.
verified_result_metric: Authors report no significant multivariate model for pain during EEG or most interference outcomes; the model for average pain intensity over the prior four weeks and a separate mood-interference model were significant. Authors describe central alpha as associated with higher pain and central delta with lower pain. No independent-validation performance metric was verified.
prediction_target: Average pain intensity in the previous four weeks and BPI pain-interference outcomes; pain during EEG was also analyzed.
validation_design: Secondary cross-sectional analysis of 36 chronic neuropathic-pain participants from Zolezzi et al. 2023. Linear/logistic regression with age and medication consideration; most nonnormal pain/interference outcomes were dichotomized at the median. No independent test sample/external validation.
open_access_status: Open-access full text at PMC.
data_evidence: The article identifies the sample as the public Zolezzi 2023 dataset, states the used data were provided by the original authors and are available in a publicly accessible database, and uses 36 patient EEG/BPI records. Mendeley v4 provides raw patient .gdf EEG and questionnaire files. Same participant cohort as Zolezzi 2023 and Ryu 2024; not a new cohort. Access-review detail: public raw EEG verified
relevance_limitations: The paper uses 5-s windows, but these are overlapping derived observations from 36 participants with person-level pain questionnaires; window count does not create independent participants. Its 250-Hz recordings, broad montage and five-minute eyes-closed state differ from three-central-channel recordings. Association and regression are not held-out prediction; regional results and outcome coding need replication.

title: Resting-state frontal electroencephalography (EEG) biomarkers for detecting the severity of chronic neuropathic pain
authors: S. Ryu, D. Gwon, C. Park, Y. Ha, M. Ahn
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Frontal EEG PAC and PAC asymmetry; spectral power asymmetry
feature_definition: Cross-frequency coupling between low-frequency phase and higher-frequency amplitude at Fp1/Fp2; left-right asymmetry features.
prediction_rationale: PAC/asymmetry may capture chronic pain severity-related nonstationary interactions missed by band power; this rationale is directly tested by the paper’s correlations and regression models.
verified_result_metric: Reported r: beta-power asymmetry −0.375; gamma-power asymmetry −0.433; low-beta-to-low-gamma coupling −0.397. Best polynomial-kernel SVR R²=0.655; no external validation verified.
prediction_target: Patient-level chronic neuropathic pain intensity from clinical ratings
validation_design: Secondary analysis of public resting EEG from 36 patients; feature-score correlations and five-model regression comparison; no external cohort/independent-site validation reported in retrieved abstract.
open_access_status: Open access (Scientific Reports full text)
data_evidence: Ryu methods explicitly identify a publicly available dataset from the cited Zolezzi study; the linked 2023 data paper reports raw resting EEG plus BPI/painDETECT reports and Mendeley repository DOI 10.17632/yj52xrfgtz.4.
relevance_limitations: The actual predictor channels are Fp1/Fp2, absent in C3/C4/Cz pipeline; frontal asymmetry cannot be recreated. Resting 5-min eyes-open data and person-level pain labels differ from five-second trial labels. Gamma feature bands may exceed 40 Hz; any >64-Hz high-gamma component is beyond 128-Hz Nyquist and current filter.

title: A comprehensive EEG dataset of laser-evoked potentials for pain research
authors: X Zhao, J Zhou, L Zhang, Y Zhuang, H Duan, S Wei, S Yao, X Lu, Y Bi, L Hu
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: high-density LEP, raw EEG and trial pain ratings
feature_definition: Dataset paper describing single-trial LEP EEG and ratings for graded laser stimuli.
prediction_rationale: Large dataset enables within- and between-person LEP feature analysis/prediction, though the paper is a resource description rather than a prediction model.
verified_result_metric: 678 healthy participants; the paper describes raw high-density EEG, 2.5–4.5-J laser stimuli, and single-trial pain ratings; no model prediction metric claimed.
prediction_target: Resource for future prediction of single-trial subjective pain rating; no predictor evaluated.
validation_design: Large-scale data resource with technical validation of EEG responses and stimulus-intensity/rating trends.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: Paper's Data Records section explicitly lists nine OpenNeuro BIDS datasets (ds005284, ds005285, ds005289, ds005286, ds005291, ds005293, ds005292, ds005280, ds005473); raw EEG plus per-trial stimulus and subjective pain ratings in EEGLAB epoch structures; preprocessed data/code also linked.
relevance_limitations: High-density resource, but recording systems/sampling rates differ by experiment; inspect each dataset's EEG JSON. Event-locked LEPs require markers/epochs; do not presume all data meet 128 Hz or C3/C4/Cz without harmonization.

title: Assessing the balance between excitation and inhibition in chronic pain through the aperiodic component of EEG
authors: Cristina Gil Ávila; Elisabeth S. May; Felix S. Bott; Laura Tiemann; Vanessa Hohn; Henrik Heitmann; Paul Theo Zebhauser; Joachim Gross; Markus Ploner
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Aperiodic exponent (aperiodic 1/f slope) and periodic/aperiodic spectral separation
feature_definition: Fit the 2–40 Hz power spectrum into aperiodic offset/exponent plus oscillatory peaks; primary feature was exponent in source-localized mPFC, with whole-brain analyses.
prediction_rationale: Aperiodic exponent was proposed as a scalable proxy for excitation/inhibition and a candidate marker of chronic pain; this study provides strong counter-evidence to simple status/intensity prediction.
verified_result_metric: Authors report robust evidence against chronic-pain/control exponent differences (all BF10 <0.22 across preregistered analyses); no relationship with pain intensity. Not classification accuracy or R².
prediction_target: Chronic pain vs healthy status and average pain intensity association; no deployed or validated predictor.
validation_design: Preregistered secondary analysis of 3 EEG cohorts; blinded analyses and multiverse; 149 chronic pain and 115 controls in final sample.
open_access_status: Open access; full article freely readable at eLife.
data_evidence: Paper reports a third cohort made public; OSF qgfma is public and links raw-data projects for Ta Dinh 2019 (g3snh) and Heitmann 2022 (gywtc). The linked preregistration states no access restrictions and identifies raw BIDS EEG URLs srpbg, a8bpx and qgfma. Data access is verified at OSF project level; cohort composition differs from final analyzed N.
relevance_limitations: Scalp EEG has 64 channels, 1000 Hz acquisition and 5-minute eyes-closed recordings before preprocessing; main mPFC/source analyses cannot be replicated with C3/C4/Cz alone. 2–40 Hz fitting is compatible with 1–40 Hz filter, but 5-second windows do not reproduce full source/aperiodic pipeline. No alpha asymmetry test.

title: Assessing the predictive value of peak alpha frequency for the sensitivity to pain
authors: E S May, L Tiemann, C Gil Ávila, F S Bott, V D Hohn, J Gross, M Ploner
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_definition: Peak frequency in the alpha range (8–13 Hz) in resting EEG, related to interindividual and intraindividual pain ratings during brief laser pain.
prediction_rationale: Evaluates whether previously proposed resting PAF biomarker generalizes to brief experimental pain.
verified_result_metric: 159 healthy participants, two sessions; multiverse/specification-curve analyses did not yield consistent evidence that PAF predicts sensitivity to brief laser pain.
prediction_target: Between-person and within-person pain sensitivity from brief laser stimuli.
validation_design: Two identical sessions with replication across sessions; 159 participants.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: Paper data statement explicitly says raw and preprocessed EEG-BIDS and analysis code are openly available at OSF s75q6.
relevance_limitations: Resting PAF needs a sufficiently long clean resting segment; a single five-second window may be unstable. Within 1–40 Hz and Nyquist, but central-only montage may omit optimal sensorimotor locations.

verified_result_metric: OSF record verifies public BrainVision EEG and 60-trial design; this is dataset metadata rather than predictor performance.

relevance_limitations: The repository is BrainVision format and channel/sample details must be checked from headers; published onset-detection target is not the same as pain intensity prediction. Harmonize sampling and montage first.

title: Peak-alpha-frequency laser pain EEG dataset (OSF s75q6)
authors: E S May et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: raw/preprocessed EEG-BIDS, resting PAF, brief laser pain ratings
feature_definition: Raw and preprocessed EEG-BIDS from 159 healthy participants with two sessions, resting state and laser-pain tasks at four intensities.
prediction_rationale: Enables replication of PAF and testing alternative EEG features against pain sensitivity.
verified_result_metric: 159 participants, two sessions; associated article reports no consistent PAF prediction for brief experimental pain.
prediction_target: Within- and between-person pain sensitivity in brief laser pain.
validation_design: Two sessions with repeated trials; repository/code publicly linked by article.
open_access_status: Public OSF project; article open access
data_evidence: May et al. explicitly state raw and preprocessed standardized EEG-BIDS and manuscript code are openly available at OSF s75q6.

title: Intra- and Inter-individual Differences of Pain - Data
authors: L Tiemann, E S May, M Ploner, F Bott
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: raw BIDS EEG, evoked and oscillatory activity, trial ratings
feature_definition: Public raw BIDS EEG from 166 healthy participants across two sessions, plus resting state and 80 laser-pain trials/session with verbal pain rating.
prediction_rationale: Supports repeated-trial modeling of moment-to-moment pain and inter-session stability.
verified_result_metric: OSF project describes 166 participants and two sessions; source article analyzes 161 in main cohort. This is dataset metadata, not an accuracy metric.
prediction_target: Verbal rating of pain after each brief laser stimulus.
validation_design: Repeated within-person sessions separated by about one month; repository has raw data for participants sub-001–sub-169 (actual enrolled n=166 per project description).
open_access_status: Public OSF project
data_evidence: Public OSF page exposes raw BIDS components and gives detailed protocol and participant count. PLOS article directly links this repository in its data availability statement.
relevance_limitations: 64-channel system; verify only selected participants and exact channel montage against the pipeline. Laser epochs need event alignment; gamma features are incompatible with 1–40-Hz passband.

title: Neural encoding of pain is robust within but unstable between individuals
authors: L Tiemann, F S Bott, E S May, M M Nickel, V D Hohn, C Gil Ávila et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: evoked N1/N2/P2 amplitudes and induced alpha/beta/gamma; Bayesian multimodel regression
feature_definition: Six canonical event-related EEG predictors related to trial pain rating after accounting for stimulus intensity.
prediction_rationale: Separates within-person moment-to-moment pain variation from between-person differences and tests replication.
verified_result_metric: 161-person primary cohort repeated after ~4 weeks and independent cohort n=111; within-person neural patterns replicated over time and across cohorts, between-person patterns repeated over time but not across cohorts. Exact R² values are not used here.
prediction_target: Single-trial verbal pain ratings (0–100) after brief painful laser stimuli.
validation_design: Repeated two-session within-person replication plus independent external cohort; Bayesian multimodel regression.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: Article data statement links standardized EEG-BIDS at OSF z2h86. OSF identifies raw BIDS for 166 healthy participants, two sessions, 80 brief laser trials/session, verbal rating each trial; do not assume the external n=111 cohort is in this repository.
relevance_limitations: 64-channel recordings and event-locked features exceed C3/C4/Cz spatial coverage; induced gamma largely outside 1–40 Hz. Accurate stimulus triggers/baseline are essential; fixed 5-s crops may obscure event morphology.

title: Determinants of Laser-Evoked EEG Responses: Pain Perception or Stimulus Saliency?
authors: G D Iannetti, N P Hughes, M C Lee, A Mouraux
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_definition: Evoked responses and synchronization following repeated noxious laser stimuli at different energies.
prediction_rationale: This is a critical validity test: evoked amplitude may reflect stimulus novelty/salience rather than pain intensity itself.
verified_result_metric: In 7 healthy participants, repetition reduced N1/N2/P2 and event-related synchronization and disrupted their relationship with pain; authors interpret responses as more salience-related than pain-specific.
prediction_target: Not a pain predictor; tests interpretation of pain-evoked response amplitudes.
validation_design: Within-subject repeated-stimulus manipulation; no out-of-sample prediction design.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: No public raw EEG repository verified.
relevance_limitations: Strong caveat for using evoked amplitudes as pain labels: stimulus salience/habituation must be controlled. Requires event timing and baseline; Cz alone loses spatial information.

title: EEG Indices of Tonic Pain-Related Activity in the Somatosensory Cortices
authors: R Dowman, H Rissacher, P Schuckers
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_definition: Scalp spectral indices during a 600-s cold-pressor pain task; alpha change in contralateral temporal electrodes and apparent gamma increase.
prediction_rationale: Tests whether sustained oscillatory changes covary with the evolving tonic pain experience.
verified_result_metric: 15 adults; 29 electrodes at 200 Hz. Authors report alpha decreases; apparent widespread gamma increase was judged likely scalp EMG artifact. No pain-prediction score verified.
prediction_target: Tonic experimental pain-related EEG activity; no validated numerical rating predictor verified.
validation_design: Within-subject cold-pressor recording with 9-point ratings each minute; no out-of-sample validation.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: No public raw dataset linked to the article verified.
relevance_limitations: 600-s tonic design, temporal electrodes, and artifact-sensitive gamma do not transfer directly to five-second C3/C4/Cz windows; preserve EMG controls.

title: Pre-stimulus alpha power affects vertex N2-P2 potentials evoked by noxious stimuli
authors: C Babiloni et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: prestimulus alpha sub-band power and evoked N2-P2
feature_definition: Single trials stratified by prestimulus alpha1/2/3 power; compare vertex N2-P2 amplitudes.
prediction_rationale: Pre-event state could explain trial-to-trial variation in pain-evoked potentials and possibly perception, but the tested outcome is evoked amplitude.
verified_result_metric: 10 participants, 30 electrodes; weak alpha-3 (about 10–12 Hz) preceded significantly larger N2-P2 than strong alpha-3 (p<.05); alpha-1/2 effects not significant. This is not a verified pain-rating prediction result.
prediction_target: Evoked N2-P2 amplitude; pain perception prediction is proposed, not established in this abstract.
validation_design: Within-subject high/low-alpha single-trial grouping; no predictive validation.
open_access_status: PubMed abstract verified; full text/OA not verified
data_evidence: No public EEG repository identified.
relevance_limitations: The reported 10–12-Hz state is within pipeline passband, but accurate stimulus/event timing and prestimulus baseline are required; the abstract does not establish subjective pain prediction.

title: Taking into account latency, amplitude, and morphology: improved estimation of single-trial ERPs by wavelet filtering and multiple linear regression
authors: L Hu, M Liang, A Mouraux, R G Wise, Y Hu, G D Iannetti
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_definition: Wavelet filtering plus multiple linear regression estimates single-trial LEP latency, amplitude, and morphology.
prediction_rationale: Single-trial N2/P2 amplitude covaries with reported pain and can be modeled as a trial-level subjective-pain marker.
verified_result_metric: In 12 healthy participants, single-trial N2/P2 amplitudes significantly correlated with pain perception; inspected abstract did not report a numeric coefficient or prediction error.
prediction_target: Trial-level subjective pain perception (relationship, not a quantified out-of-sample predictor in the verified abstract).
validation_design: Human laser-pain study; n=12. No independent external validation verified.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: No paper-linked public raw EEG repository was verified.
relevance_limitations: LEP is stimulus-locked and vertex-heavy; the project needs event markers and a pre-stimulus baseline. 5-s windows can contain the response but are not equivalent to the paper's epoched single-trial analysis.

title: Gamma-Band Oscillations in the Primary Somatosensory Cortex—A Direct and Obligatory Correlate of Subjective Pain Intensity
authors: Z G Zhang, L Hu, Y S Hung, A Mouraux, G D Iannetti
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_definition: Pain-evoked 30–100 Hz oscillatory activity over primary somatosensory cortex, assessed against subjective ratings under repeated-stimulus conditions.
prediction_rationale: The article reports GBO tracks trial pain intensity even when repeated stimulation changes salience-related evoked responses.
verified_result_metric: Authors report GBO intensity relates to subjective pain intensity despite repetition; no numeric predictive accuracy verified in the inspected record.
prediction_target: Subjective pain intensity on laser trials.
validation_design: Human laser-pain experiment (reported n=7); within-study relationship, no external validation verified.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: No linked public EEG repository verified.
relevance_limitations: Most of the 30–100-Hz band lies above the pipeline's 40-Hz low-pass and part lies above the 64-Hz Nyquist at Fs=128; this feature is therefore largely not recoverable. Source/cortical localization also exceeds C3/C4/Cz.

title: Tonic pain and continuous EEG: Prediction of subjective pain perception by alpha-1 power during stimulation and at rest
authors: R R Nir, A Sinai, R Moont, E Harari, D Yarnitsky
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: alpha-1 power at rest and during tonic stimulation
feature_definition: Continuous EEG alpha-1 power (individualized low-alpha range) during rest, warmth, and noxious stimulation, related to numeric pain score.
prediction_rationale: Resting alpha-1 may predict subsequent tonic-pain sensitivity; stimulation alpha-1 tracks concurrent pain ratings.
verified_result_metric: 18 volunteers, five-minute conditions; temporal scalp alpha-1 negatively correlated with concurrent NPS and resting alpha-1 with subsequent noxious NPS (p≤.04); full-text effect sizes unavailable in inspected abstract.
prediction_target: Subjective tonic pain numeric pain score during stimulation and after rest.
validation_design: Within-subject rest/warm/noxious continuous EEG; independent predictive validation not verified.
open_access_status: Abstract readable; full text open access not verified
data_evidence: No public repository found in the inspected abstract record.
relevance_limitations: Temporal scalp distribution and sustained 5-min contexts differ from central C3/C4/Cz; five-second crops do not reproduce resting-state or tonic trajectories.

title: A novel approach to predict subjective pain perception from single-trial laser-evoked potentials
authors: G Huang, P Xiao, Y S Hung, G D Iannetti, Z G Zhang, L Hu
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: single-trial LEP features; common spatial patterns and multiple linear regression
feature_definition: CSP plus MLR estimate trial-level LEP features; Naive Bayes classifies low/high pain and linear regression estimates 0–10 pain rating.
prediction_rationale: Directly trains single-trial LEP features against participants' subjective pain reports.
verified_result_metric: Publisher abstract reports binary accuracy 86.3±8.4% within-person and 80.3±8.5% cross-person; continuous MAE 1.031±0.136 and 1.821±0.202 respectively. Publisher abstract verified; full primary text not accessed here.
prediction_target: Low/high pain classification and continuous single-trial subjective rating (0–10).
validation_design: Within-individual and cross-individual prediction; no independent external cohort verified in inspected abstract.
open_access_status: Publisher abstract verified; full text appears access-restricted, OA not verified
data_evidence: No public raw EEG repository linked to this paper was verified; do not infer that a later public dataset is this study's data.
relevance_limitations: CSP uses spatial patterns beyond three central channels; LEPs require precise triggers and trial epochs. Verify full methods, subject count, and leakage-safe cross-person split before using reported scores.

title: Brain oscillations differentially encode noxious stimulus intensity and pain intensity
authors: M M Nickel, E S May, L Tiemann, P Schmidt, M Postorino, S T Dinh, J Gross, M Ploner
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: tonic alpha/beta desynchronization and gamma power
feature_definition: EEG oscillatory power during 10-min painful heat; source-space alpha/beta related to physical stimulus intensity, medial prefrontal gamma to pain ratings.
prediction_rationale: Separating physical stimulus intensity from subjective pain is central to pain prediction; alpha/beta and gamma showed different relationships to those targets.
verified_result_metric: 39 healthy participants; stimulus-intensity links included alpha t=-6.9, p<.001, and pain-rating links included prefrontal gamma t=4.1/4.8, p<.001. These are association statistics, not held-out prediction metrics.
prediction_target: Continuous pain rating, distinct from physical stimulus intensity.
validation_design: Within-subject continuous 10-min heat, left/right hand; linear mixed models; no independent validation verified.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: No public data repository tied to this 2017 paper verified; do not substitute another Nickel-group OSF dataset.
relevance_limitations: Long tonic protocol and source-localized medial prefrontal target are not captured by five-second C3/C4/Cz windows. Gamma band and prefrontal regions are largely outside the project's 1–40-Hz/sparse-channel coverage.

title: Magnitude and Temporal Variability of Inter-stimulus EEG Modulate the Linear Relationship Between Laser-Evoked Potentials and Fast-Pain Perception
authors: L Li, G Huang, Q Lin, J Liu, S Zhang, Z Zhang
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: inter-stimulus EEG magnitude (RMS) and temporal variability (nMSSD); LEP N2-P2
feature_definition: Between-stimulus broadband/frequency-band RMS and normalized mean-square successive difference; LEP amplitude-pain linear model.
prediction_rationale: Interstimulus state features index between-person differences in the LEP–pain mapping, enabling individualized cross-person modeling.
verified_result_metric: Authors report individualized cross-person fast-pain MAE 1.19±0.35 versus conventional cross-person LEP MAE 1.36±0.51 (paired p=.002). Alpha-2 nMSSD correlated with LEP model slope; interstimulus RMS with intercept.
prediction_target: Fast-pain subjective rating from single-trial LEP, with cross-person transfer.
validation_design: 34 healthy participants; test-person selection/weighting by interstimulus EEG; reported comparison to conventional cross-individual predictor.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: No public raw data URL verified in inspected article excerpts.
relevance_limitations: This asks for between-stimulus signal and event-locked LEP windows, not just fixed continuous 5-s features. Broad scalp RMS feature needs channel coverage; the alpha-2 band is within 1–40 Hz.

title: Brain dysfunction in chronic pain patients assessed by resting-state electroencephalography
authors: Vanessa D. Hohn et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Phase-based functional connectivity: PLV and dwPLI; amplitude-envelope correlation comparator
feature_definition: Sensor-pair connectivity estimated from phase synchrony (PLV/dwPLI); chronic pain resting-state EEG compared with healthy controls.
prediction_rationale: Reported pain-control connectivity differences can motivate a participant-level group classifier, but sensitivity/specificity and clinical validity need independent validation.
verified_result_metric: SVM patient/control accuracy 57% (above chance as reported); corrected comparisons found increased theta and >60-Hz frontal connectivity. This is classification accuracy, not variance explained.
prediction_target: Chronic pain versus healthy-control group; not continuous pain severity
validation_design: 101 chronic-pain patients plus healthy controls; resting-state feature comparison and SVM classification. Data/scripts available on request, not a public validation set.
open_access_status: Open-access full text (CC BY 4.0; PMC)
data_evidence: Article data-availability statement explicitly says all scripts and data are available on request.
relevance_limitations: Important feature-family precedent, but frontal topography is unavailable in C3/C4/Cz; gamma above 64 Hz exceeds 128-Hz Nyquist and >40 Hz is removed by pipeline filter. Do not interpret 57% classification as variance or regression performance.

title: Markers of Central Neuropathic Pain in Higuchi Fractal Analysis of EEG Signals From People With Spinal Cord Injury
authors: Keri Anderson, Cristian Chirion, Matthew Fraser, Mariel Purcell, Sebastian Stein, Aleksandra Vuckovic
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_definition: Non-oscillatory HFD computed from EEG during imagined movement; the study tests group differences and machine-learning classification in chronic/subacute spinal-cord-injury pain cohorts.
prediction_rationale: Authors investigate HFD as a prognostic/diagnostic feature for central neuropathic pain after SCI; their interpretation is not general nociceptive pain-intensity prediction.
verified_result_metric: Abstract reports transferable classifiers with >80% accuracy for chronic-SCI groups using a single EEG channel; HFD differs across chronic and 6-month follow-up groups. Metric is classification accuracy, not variance explained or pain-intensity correlation.
prediction_target: Chronic central neuropathic pain group status and later CNP development after SCI.
validation_design: Two datasets: chronic groups (10 able-bodied, 10 SCI+CNP, 10 SCI without CNP) and subacute SCI follow-up (N=20; 10 developed CNP); bootstrapped group tests and transferable classifier. Raw dataset availability not verified.
open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC; Frontiers open-access article.
data_url: No linked public raw EEG repository verified.
data_evidence: Paper describes existing EEG datasets but this research pass did not verify a public repository tied to them; candidate only for public-data criterion.
relevance_limitations: Frontal effects/channels and imagined-movement epochs may be essential; frontal sensors are absent from C3/C4/Cz and movement event timing is not represented by generic 5-s windows. Clinical SCI neuropathic pain is not equivalent to acute pain-intensity rating.

title: Accurate classification of pain experiences using wearable electroencephalography in adolescents with and without chronic musculoskeletal pain
authors: Elizabeth F. Teel et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Directed PLI (dPLI) and wPLI were calculated; only dPLI was retained in reported classification feature set; other entropy/graph features were also tested
feature_definition: wPLI summarizes weighted non-zero-lag phase coupling; dPLI captures direction of phase leads/lags. Paper reports wPLI removed before classification; dPLI retained.
prediction_rationale: dPLI’s reported classification performance is relevant to directional phase-based connectivity; it does not establish predictive utility for wPLI.
verified_result_metric: Separate SVM baseline-vs-CPT classification: chronic-pain cohort 75.2% accuracy (95% CI 71.4–77.1%); no-pain-vs-pain classification SVM 75.6% (95% CI 71.9–77.6%). dPLI/PE/peak frequency significant individually; wPLI excluded, so no wPLI metric.
prediction_target: Baseline versus cold-pressor-task EEG condition (separately in control and chronic-pain adolescents); no-pain vs pain group-label result is also reported.
validation_design: 19-channel EEG, 10-s epochs, SVM/logistic models; paper reports test/train performance. External validation not verified.
open_access_status: Open-access full article (Frontiers)
data_url: Not provided as a repository link
data_evidence: Article data-availability statement says raw supporting data ‘will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation’; no public repository link verified.
relevance_limitations: Adolescent cold-pressor paradigm and 10-s epochs differ from 5-s chronic adult signals. wPLI was removed from classifier; reported accuracy does not evidence wPLI prediction. Task condition confounds subjective pain; no repository link and data are on request.

title: Electroencephalography Signatures for Conditioned Pain Modulation and Pain Perception in Nonspecific Chronic Low Back Pain—An Exploratory Study
authors: Paulo E. P. Teixeira et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: EEG spectral signal strength (relative power), not CVUE/nonlinear complexity
feature_definition: Resting-state absolute/relative delta–beta power per electrode, using 5-s FFT windows with 50% overlap; 30-patient cross-sectional chronic low-back-pain sample.
prediction_rationale: Authors report central delta/theta relative power associations with self-reported pain when controlling for depression; transferable baseline signal-strength features, not a validated predictor.
verified_result_metric: Authors say significant delta/theta EEG models explained approximately 20% of pain-score variability; separate CPM–pain model R²=0.12 and nonsignificant (p=.12). The EEG result is exploratory, not held-out accuracy.
prediction_target: Seven-day average self-reported low-back-pain VAS; CPM was a separate target.
validation_design: N=30 cross-sectional exploratory regressions with feature screening/backward selection; no external test set. EEG model includes mood/QST covariates.
open_access_status: Freely readable full text in PMC.
data_url: No linked public EEG repository verified.
data_evidence: Inspected full-text excerpt documents study and results but no verified linked public raw-EEG repository; source tables are not raw EEG.
relevance_limitations: 5-s windows and 1–40 Hz match the current pipeline; central channels include C3/C4/Cz, but paper also uses frontal/parietal sensors unavailable here. Tests relative power, not variance/CVUE/HFD/PE; no public raw data verified.

title: Towards the Objective Identification of the Presence of Pain Based on Electroencephalography Signals’ Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept
authors: M K Segning et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: CVUE (coefficient of variation of upper envelope), alpha/beta/gamma
feature_definition: Standard deviation divided by mean of the upper Hilbert-envelope distribution, computed for band-limited EEG features.
prediction_rationale: CVUE is proposed as a signal descriptor that separates pain presence from control state.
verified_result_metric: Four fibromyalgia patients and seven healthy capsaicin-pain controls; beta CVUE increased at FC5; authors report no correlation between beta CVUE and pain-intensity ratings/task performance. No predictive accuracy established.
prediction_target: Pain presence/group condition, not pain intensity regression.
validation_design: Small proof-of-concept comparison of fibromyalgia and experimentally induced pain with healthy baseline; no independent test cohort.
open_access_status: Open-access full text
data_evidence: No public EEG repository verified.
relevance_limitations: FC5/T7 are absent from C3/C4/Cz; EEG was downsampled to 128 Hz, but paper's beta features (and its gamma to 43 Hz) need matching band definitions. Very small cohort and null pain-rating correlation limit direct predictive use.

title: A systematic review of neurophysiological sensing for the assessment of acute pain
authors: Fernandez Rojas et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Review of EEG response strength/variability and prediction designs
feature_definition: Synthesizes acute-pain neurophysiological sensing, EEG feature engineering, and classification/regression studies from 2013–July 2022.
prediction_rationale: Inference: useful as a map of candidate labels, feature definitions and study designs; does not itself validate a signal-strength feature.
verified_result_metric: Review included 48 studies overall; no single pooled EEG variance/SNR effect or pooled prediction metric verified.
prediction_target: Acute pain assessment across reviewed studies.
validation_design: Systematic literature review; search July 2022; review-level evidence, not an independent validation cohort.
open_access_status: Open-access full text (PMC; CC BY 4.0).
data_evidence: Review article; no new raw EEG data.
relevance_limitations: Broad sensing review includes non-EEG modalities and feature-focused studies; use only EEG-specific entries and do not treat review totals as EEG-only.

title: External validation of binary machine learning models for pain intensity perception classification from EEG in healthy individuals
authors: Tyler Mari; Oda Asgard; Jessica Henderson; et al.
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Single-trial peri-stimulus time-frequency EEG features; not an alpha-only spectral test
feature_definition: Feature-selected time-frequency values from all electrodes during high/low pneumatic pressure pain; frequencies/electrodes span more than alpha.
prediction_rationale: Independent-sample validation tests whether EEG features generalize for subjective high/low experimental pain intensity; it is contextual prediction evidence, not evidence that alpha power alone predicts pain.
verified_result_metric: Random Forest accuracy: 73.18% cross-validation, 68.32% external validation 1, 60.42% external validation 2. These are classification accuracies, not R² or correlations.
prediction_target: Binary low vs high experimental pain intensity.
validation_design: Study 1 n=25 train/cross-validation; study 2 n=15 independent participants used for two external validations (one same stimulation, one new parameters).
open_access_status: Open access; freely readable PMC full text and publisher page.
data_evidence: Article states EEG is freely available at OSF uqt9z, but fetched OSF project page shows “No files are available at this time”; availability of raw EEG could not be verified, so it is not counted as public EEG.
relevance_limitations: 1000 Hz acquisition, high/low pressure event markers, peri-stimulus time-frequency features, and frontal/central/parietal electrodes; current C3/C4/Cz-only, 1–40 Hz, five-second features cannot reproduce event-locked multichannel features. No alpha-specific feature ranking/result verified.

title: The Analysis of Spontaneous Electroencephalogram (EEG) in Chronic Low Back Pain Patients Compared with Healthy Subjects
authors: Sanaz Bemani; Javad Sarrafzadeh; Shohreh Noorizadeh Dehkordi; Saeed Talebian; Reza Salehi; Jamileh Zarei
review_level: Study/access evidence reviewed; see individual limitations
feature_family: Relative and absolute band power; alpha relative power
feature_definition: Welch/FFT power spectral density; alpha defined 8.0–13.9 Hz and relative power is band absolute power divided by total power.
prediction_rationale: Alpha relative power may separate chronic-low-back-pain cases from controls, but the paper tested group differences rather than training a predictive model; pain-intensity prediction was not supported by its reported correlation analysis.
verified_result_metric: Among 30 CLBP and 30 matched controls, alpha relative power was significantly higher in CLBP at eyes-open rest and lumbar flexion (P<0.05). Authors describe subjective pain vs EEG frequency-power correlation as very weak/negligible; numeric r and prediction accuracy not verified.
prediction_target: CLBP/control group difference; secondary association with NRS pain severity, not validated prediction.
validation_design: Cross-sectional case-control comparison; paired t-tests and Pearson correlations; 30 CLBP plus 30 controls.
open_access_status: Open access; freely readable PMC full text.
